ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two op-amps on the left side of the circuit, and one op-amp on the right side. The input terminal of the upper-left op-amp is connected to VIN through R1, the feedback resistor is R2, and the non-inverting terminal is grounded, so it is an inverting amplifier; its output is denoted as Va. The lower-left op-amp has its non-inverting terminal driven by VIN, and its inverting terminal is connected to ground through R1 and receives feedback from the output through R2, so it is a non-inverting amplifier; its output is denoted as Vb. The non-inverting terminal of the right-side op-amp is grounded, and the two left-side outputs are respectively connected to its inverting terminal through equal input resistors R3, with feedback resistor R4, so it is an inverting summer. Reasoning: For the upper-left inverting amplifier, Va = -(R2/R1)VIN. For the lower-left non-inverting amplifier, Vb = (1 + R2/R1)VIN. The right-side inverting summer satisfies VOUT = -(R4/R3)(Va + Vb). Substitution gives Va + Vb = -(R2/R1)VIN + (1 + R2/R1)VIN = VIN. Therefore VOUT = -(R4/R3)VIN, so VOUT/VIN = -R4/R3.
